references.text: The disciples answered exactly as Jesus instructed them: 'The Lord has need of it' ([ref:Luk 19:34|Luke 19:34]). This shows the fulfillment of Jesus' words in verse 31.

Mark's parallel account contains the same instruction from Jesus about what the disciples should say if anyone asks why they are untying the colt: 'The Lord has need of it' ([ref:Mark 11:3|Mark 11:3]).
Matthew's parallel account where Jesus instructs the disciples to say that 'the Lord has need of them' if anyone asks ([ref:Matt 21:3|Matthew 21:3]).

The immediate context where Jesus sends two of his disciples to fetch the colt and gives them detailed instructions ([ref:Luk 19:28-30|Luke 19:28-30]). Verse 31 continues the instruction with what they should say if anyone asks.
Jesus is called 'Lord and Teacher' by his disciples ([ref:Joh 13:13|John 13:13]). The term 'the Lord' (ὁ κύριος) in Luke 19:31 emphasizes Jesus' authority and dominion, even over material things.
'The earth is the Lord's, and everything in it' ([ref:Sal 24:1|Psalm 24:1]). Jesus' request to use the colt reflects the Lord's sovereign ownership over all creation.

A similar pattern where the disciples are sent out by Jesus and find everything exactly as he had said beforehand, this time in preparation for the Passover meal ([ref:Luk 22:13|Luke 22:13]). This demonstrates Jesus' prophetic foreknowledge.
